problem: Determine if the vector $u$ lies on the plane $Π:r=sb+tc$, $t,s\in R$, where  $b=⟨-1,4,3⟩$, $c=⟨1,-6,-7⟩$, and  $u=⟨1,-10,-15⟩.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $s\cdot t$ from the decomposition $u=sb+tc.$
worked_solution:
By definition, $u\in Π$ if there exist $t$ and $s$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc & =u \\ s[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -6 \\ -7\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -10 \\ -15\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-s+t=1 \\ 4s-6t=-10 \\ 3s-7t=-15\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ 4 & -6 & -10 \\ 3 & -7 & -15\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & -6 \\ 3 & -7 & -15\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & -4 & -12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}-s+t=1 \\ -2t=-6 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get

$$
-2t=-6\,⟹\,t=3.
$$

Substituting into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-s+t & =1 \\ -s+3 & =1 \\ -s & =-2 \\ s & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we found a solution $s=2,\,t=3,$ we conclude that $u$ does indeed lie on the plane $Π.$ In fact, we have

$$
u=2b+3c.
$$

Finally, $s\cdot t=2\cdot 3=6.$
